posts:
David Kochie challenges the RBA to name government spending as the true driver of Australian inflation.
Evidence: public spending, rate hikes, mortgage squeeze🌐
#Aletheia #Australia #Economy

Media personality David Kochie urged the RBA to call out federal and state government spending as the primary inflation driver.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Good Preference

While public spending contributes, global supply chains, utility indexing, and wage pressures also fuel inflation, making rate hikes a blunt instrument.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.47, -0.58) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Oversimplifying inflation drivers deflects systemic accountability onto political finger-pointing.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.8, z: 2)

- Media Rhetoric: COND (-0.47, 0.40) — Sharp public pressure, but oversimplifies monetary policy.
- Central Bank Policy: COND (0.20, -0.40) — Holds rates steady but balances opposing political currents.
As major banks forecast a cash rate rise to 4.60%, commentators like Kochie are turning public frustration toward government-regulated price pressures.

The Poison:
Reducing complex macroeconomic inflation drivers to pure partisan political point-scoring.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing political grievance (WHO) with monetary policy mechanics (HOW).

Social Physics Analysis:
Commentators run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, utilizing public economic anxiety as a pretext to target political opponents while ignoring broader structural pricing dynamics.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Blaming politicians fails to stop rate hikes.

The Unavoidable Truth: Government-regulated fees and public spending do contribute significantly to sticky inflation.

The Unavoidable Lie: Blaming one side of politics stops the RBA from raising mortgage rates.

Alethekanon:
Fiscal friction gets weaponized in media narratives while central bankers ignore political noise.

Awwthekanon:
Families are carrying such heavy burdens right now; everyone deserves clear answers and relief.

Brothekanon:
Kochie calling out Canberra is great TV, but it won't stop your mortgage going up next week.

Spirithekanon:
"The one who states his case first seems right, until the other comes and examines him." Proverbs 18:17 COND
Loud media finger-pointing provides theatrical catharsis, but ignores the interlocking forces driving economic strain.
